paths.description: Storefront homepage, representing discovery, recommendations, global navigation, consent, responsive layout, and initial load.
Dota 2 detail page, representing a product entity, commercial information, media, and the primary acquire/play journey.
Search results for “cozy”, representing listing/filter discovery and query-result navigation.
Sign-in page, representing account authentication, labels, autofill, and credential assistance.
Unknown route, representing HTTP/not-found recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The storefront is hard-coded dark rather than adapting to the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Desktop and prefers-color-scheme:dark screenshots render the same dark palette, and the DOM probe found no preference-driven theming signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light and dark tokens, retaining the current palette as the dark branch.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found no view-transition usage on a multi-route storefront.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for carousel/state changes and cross-document transitions for compatible store routes, with fallbacks.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not respond to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The long storefront screenshot shows static navigation, and the DOM/CSS probe found no modern scroll-state mechanism.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state container queries or a restrained shrinking-header treatment to preserve orientation while maximizing content.

findings.summary: Menus and overlays use manually positioned legacy containers rather than anchored positioning.
findings.evidence: The DOM contains fixed custom responsive menu/search overlays and no popover or anchor-positioning primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for menus and contextual surfaces.

findings.summary: The cookie prompt obscures primary content on every representative page.
findings.evidence: Homepage, product, search, and login screenshots show a large fixed consent panel covering featured content, product information, results, or the sign-in form.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface with equal choices and preserve access to the primary task.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is an ad-hoc fixed div rather than a semantic dialog/popover.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero dialog and popover elements while screenshots and DOM show #cookiePrefPopup as a fixed custom container.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the consent surface with an appropriate dialog/popover primitive, focus handling, and declarative dismissal where suitable.

findings.summary: Reusable storefront components rely on viewport-era responsive CSS rather than container queries.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM/CSS probe found no @container usage despite cards and navigation being reused in substantially different widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container-type and size/style queries for reusable cards, carousels, and navigation modules.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are too small even though keyboard focus is visible.
findings.evidence: The active probe counted 32 visible links/controls under 24 px in at least one dimension; the focused sign-in link did receive a browser outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase compact targets to at least 24 by 24 CSS px, preferably 44 by 44 for primary touch controls, without removing focus styles.

findings.summary: Unknown routes silently redirect to the storefront instead of explaining the failure.
findings.evidence: Navigating to /nonexistent-web-uplift-test produced the ordinary homepage with no not-found message or recovery context.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 state with a clear explanation, search, home link, and relevant recovery suggestions.

findings.summary: Lab Core Web Vitals are poor on the storefront.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 22.4 s, TBT 430 ms, and CLS 0.129 (performance 43); the independent trace measured LCP 2.16 s but still observed blocking tasks, indicating substantial condition sensitivity.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reduce initial bytes and scripting, and reserve dynamic layout space; verify under mobile throttling and field data.

findings.summary: Homepage and product layouts shift beyond the good CLS threshold.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 layout observer measured CLS 0.168 on home and 0.157 on the product page; 99 of 100 images lacked both dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image/carousel/consent space with dimensions or aspect-ratio and use stable font fallbacks.

findings.summary: Initial load performs avoidable long main-thread tasks.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded two long tasks, longest 107 ms, with 71 ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 430 ms TBT under throttling.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks, schedule non-critical work by priority, and defer below-fold carousel initialization.

findings.summary: The initial storefront payload is excessive and has a long render-blocking chain.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 116 requests and 8.52 MB transferred, including 6.63 MB images, 14 parser-blocking stylesheets and synchronous legacy scripts; several fonts/assets lacked cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce critical CSS, defer non-critical scripts, modernize font delivery, preload only the LCP resource, and enforce durable immutable caching for versioned assets.

findings.summary: The page ships over a megabyte of unused JavaScript plus substantial unused CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,072 KiB unused JavaScript and 334 KiB unused CSS, including chunks with more than 99% waste.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split bundles, conditionally import carousel/recommendation features, and remove legacy or duplicate dependencies.

findings.summary: Accessible names, roles, and alternatives are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed aria-required-children, image-alt, label-content-name-mismatch, and link-name; the image audit found 19 images without alt and the probe found five unlabeled controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix ARIA ownership, provide matching accessible names and labels, and add meaningful or empty alt text as appropriate.

findings.summary: Some text and controls do not meet minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the color-contrast audit; forced-colors remained usable but does not remedy default-palette contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground and surface tokens to WCAG AA contrast and retest default and forced-color modes.

findings.summary: Heading and ARIA structure do not provide a robust page outline.
findings.evidence: The homepage has no h1 and only footer h3 headings; Lighthouse also found malformed required ARIA children. Focus itself remained visibly outlined.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a page-level h1, logical section headings and landmarks, and repair composite widget roles while preserving visible focus.

findings.summary: Compact targets reduce touch and zoom usability.
findings.evidence: The probe counted 32 visible targets below 24 px in one dimension. Mobile layouts reflow without horizontal overflow, but target sizing remains inadequate.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target hit areas and verify at 200% zoom and narrow reflow.

findings.summary: Image markup is unstable and sometimes distorted.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 99 of 100 images without both dimensions, 29 oversized images, and Lighthouse failed image-aspect-ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, preserve natural ratios, and provide responsive sources.

findings.summary: Key templates lack meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: The live homepage probe returned no meta description; search and sign-in DOM snapshots also lack one, although product detail has a description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add unique, useful descriptions to the homepage and index templates where public discovery is intended.

findings.summary: The advertised sitemap endpoint is not a sitemap.
findings.evidence: GET /sitemap.xml returns 302 to the homepage HTML, and robots.txt declares no Sitemap line. Canonical and robots checks otherwise passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a real sitemap index, reference it from robots.txt, and retain per-template canonical URLs.

findings.summary: Product and storefront entities have social metadata but no structured data.
findings.evidence: DOM snapshots found Open Graph tags but zero JSON-LD blocks on the homepage and Dota 2 product detail.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite and Product/Offer JSON-LD matching visible names, prices, availability, and canonical URLs.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie posture remain weaker than expected.
findings.evidence: Final response uses HSTS and frame-ancestors, but CSP permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. The sessionid cookie is SameSite=None and JavaScript-readable, and timezoneOffset was not Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Move to nonce/hash-based CSP without unsafe-eval, document any intentionally script-readable CSRF token, use the narrowest SameSite policy, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure.

findings.summary: The sign-in surface offers password/QR methods but no detectable passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login DOM probe found no WebAuthn/PublicKeyCredential signal or passkey copy.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys/WebAuthn as a first-class phishing-resistant sign-in and reauthentication option.

findings.summary: Several defensive headers are absent or too permissive.
findings.evidence: Header evidence indicates no X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy on the main response; CSP includes unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. HSTS and clickjacking protection are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, a deliberate Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and harden CSP with nonces/hashes and Trusted Types where feasible.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling hides the error state.
findings.evidence: An unknown URL resolves to an ordinary storefront screen with no failure status or recovery explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve intentional 404/5xx templates with meaningful status codes, search, retry/home actions, and retained context.

findings.summary: Sign-in inputs do not expose standard autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: The login probe found the account-name and password fields with empty autocomplete values, while the search field explicitly uses autocomplete=off.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username and current-password (plus webauthn when passkeys are available) and keep labels programmatically associated.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes several megabytes.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 6.63 MB of images; the image audit found 87 legacy-format images, 29 oversized images, 34 without responsive sources, and 43 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold media, and right-size artwork to its rendered slot.

findings.summary: Below-fold work and resources are loaded eagerly.
findings.evidence: The initial page makes 116 requests; 43 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded and Lighthouse reports large unused JS/CSS payloads.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer below-fold feeds and media until near viewport, conditionally load feature code, and cancel work no longer relevant.

findings.summary: The storefront has no effective initial media budget.
findings.evidence: Initial transfer is 8.52 MB, of which 8.15 MB comes from Steam CDN origins and 6.63 MB is images; individual decorative images exceed 1.1 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-template byte/request budgets, cap carousel media, and enforce optimized formats and caching in the asset pipeline.

findings.summary: The public commerce surface exposes no structured agent capability contract.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse agentic browsing scored 27; the DOM has no WebMCP tools and product actions are only encoded in presentation markup.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose safe, user-mediated WebMCP capabilities for search, product inspection, cart intent, and account-safe actions, with clear confirmation boundaries.
